app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

insights: Service 'image-provider' has a single backing pod: image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-xbfnd (status: Running) — i.e., only one replica available to serve traffic

Pod logs (last 500 lines) show frequent successful HTTP 200 responses for many image GET requests and contain no ERROR/WARN entries, stack traces, 'timeout' messages, or other signs of blocked/stuck threads
There is no evidence in the pod's logs of internal blocking I/O, crashes, or CrashLoopBackOff behavior — the hypothesis that the image-provider process itself was blocked or unhealthy is disproven
Log entries show many large static asset responses (image payload sizes often 100KB–350KB), which increases per-request work and can expose capacity or network bottlenecks

Given the single replica and clean application logs, the most likely causes are limited capacity (only one pod handling all requests) or external/network/proxy-induced latency (e.g., frontend-proxy, network throughput, or client-side delays) rather than an internal application failure

Actionable next steps (inferred): scale image-provider replicas to increase capacity, measure network/proxy latency (frontend-proxy traces/metrics), and capture request-level timings (APM or access logs with durations) to isolate whether latency originates in the cluster network/proxy or client path
